tasks.q: Why are standards needed in computing?
a: So hardware and software from different manufacturers can work together
To stop people making new products
tasks.fb: Standards mean a laptop from one company can use Wi-Fi from another.

tasks.q: Which of these is a standard?
tasks.fb: USB sets rules that every maker follows for connectors and data transfer.

a: A set of rules for how devices communicate on a network
tasks.fb: Both ends must follow the same protocol to understand each other.

tasks.q: Why must both devices use the same protocol?
a: So each can understand the data the other sends
So they have the same MAC address
So they can share a screen
tasks.fb: It's like two people agreeing to speak the same language.

a: Requesting and delivering web pages between browsers and web servers
tasks.fb: HTTP delivers HTML files from web servers to browsers.

tasks.q: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?
a: Encryption and authentication of the data between client and server

tasks.q: Match each email protocol to its job.
pairs: Sends email to a mail server
Retrieves email from a mail server
Retrieves email and manages mailboxes on the server
tasks.fb: IMAP keeps mail on the server, so every device sees the same inbox.

tasks.q: Which protocol keeps your emails in sync across your phone and laptop?
tasks.fb: IMAP manages mail on the server rather than just downloading it.
File Transfer Protocol does exactly what its name says.

tasks.q: Which protocol would upload a website's files to a web server?
tasks.fb: FTP is the classic way to upload web pages for hosting.

a: Makes sure all the packets arrive without errors and in the right order
tasks.fb: If a packet goes missing, TCP gets it sent again.

a: Routes packets across networks to the right address
tasks.fb: IP handles addressing and routing; TCP handles reliability.

tasks.q: Match each protocol to its description.
pairs: Requests and delivers web pages (HTML files)
Web pages with encryption and authentication
Sends email to a mail server
Retrieves email from a mail server
Retrieves email and manages mailboxes on the server
tasks.fb: Learn these eight: exam questions often ask you to name the protocol for a job.

info.title: USB-C
info.text: A standard can become law: from the end of 2024, new phones sold in the EU had to use USB-C charging ports.

info.title: Who writes the rules?
info.text: Organisations such as the IEEE and the IETF agree networking standards, so that companies around the world build compatible products.

info.title: Port numbers
info.text: Protocols use numbered 'ports'. Web servers usually listen on port 80 for HTTP and port 443 for HTTPS.

info.title: The @ symbol
info.text: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971 and chose the @ symbol to separate the user's name from their computer's name.

info.title: FTP is fading
info.text: Plain FTP sends passwords unencrypted, so many hosts now use secure versions, such as SFTP, instead.

info.title: Packets take different routes
info.text: The packets for one web page can travel by completely different routes. TCP puts them back in order when they arrive.
